topic: Orangetheory Fitness Launches OTconnect for Apple Watch

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Orangetheory Fitness Launches OTconnect for Apple Watch

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Orangetheory Fitness (OTF) is letting members use their own Apple Watch to connect to its in-studio performance-tracking platform. The option, called OTconnect for Apple Watch, becomes available October 23 at participating U.S. studios, the company announced. The integration is part of OTconnect, Orangetheory’s proprietary connected technology platform, which tracks performance in real time and delivers post-class results. Members pay a one-time $99 connection fee to pair their watch with the system. Once connected, they can start their workout on the Apple Watch before class and see heart rate, heart rate zones, calories burned and Splat Points on the wrist during the session. Afterward, they can review a performance summary in the Orangetheory app on the watch. More workout data and personalized insights are available through the OTF app and in a post-class email. The feature works with newer Apple Watch models. It requires watchOS 11.6 or later and is compatible with Apple Watch Series 6 and newer, Apple Watch SE and newer, and Apple Watch Ultra and newer. Members who connect a watch also receive up to two free months of Apple Music and Apple Fitness+. Orangetheory’s own performance monitor, OTconnect Beat , remains available in studios and online. According to the company, the two options give members more choice in how they connect to and track their data.

en.headline: Orangetheory Fitness Launches OTconnect for Apple Watch

topic: Fitness International’s Club Studio Expands in LA

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Fitness International’s Club Studio Expands in LA

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The premium fitness concept from the parent company of LA Fitness is adding clubs in Beverly Hills and Santa Monica as it pursues ambitious nationwide growth Club Studio, the premium, group fitness-oriented concept from LA Fitness parent company Fitness International, is expanding its Los Angeles footprint with plans for two new locations in Beverly Hills and Santa Monica. The new clubs will be located at 8484 Wilshire Boulevard in Beverly Hills and 2001 Wilshire Boulevard in Santa Monica, marking Club Studio’s second location in the latter city. Club Studio currently operates a handful of clubs in the Southern California area, according to its website. Both new clubs will feature Club Studio ‘s signature combination of boutique-style group fitness, premium strength and cardio equipment, personal training and recovery amenities, bringing multiple fitness and wellness offerings together under one roof. The company hasn’t yet announced opening dates or additional details about the clubs’ size and specific amenities. “The communities surrounding these locations are exactly the type of markets where Club Studio thrives,” said Nick Roberts, chief real estate officer at Fitness International.

topic: WILDE Lands $40M to Scale Protein Snacks

facts.label: Story
facts.value: WILDE Lands $40M to Scale Protein Snacks

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Real deal. What’s happening: WILDE, maker of chicken-derived chips, secured $40M from S2G Investments to fuel retail expansion and bring new protein-packed snacks to market. New chew. WILDE’s proprietary production crisps chicken breast, egg whites, and bone broth into chips and crackers, packing 10+ grams of protein per serving — ~5x more than traditional, carb-heavy salty snacks. Founded in 2015, it has benefited from consumer proteinmaxxing , reaching 30K+ retailers nationwide and notching $100M+ in sales last year. With a new 130K-sq-ft facility expanding capacity sixfold, it’s eyeing a bigger slice of the $5.5B meat snack market. Meat market. Atop the US food guide and untouched by the whey shortage , meat snacks are a growth market. But, as incumbents cede share to cleaner brands, sourcing is the next battleground. Selling 2M meat sticks daily and projecting ~$900M in ’26 sales, Chomps recently entered breakfast, while Archer secured $100M to scale up. Equip and Lineage build bars with beef-derived ingredients, while UK-based WILDE rival The Curators courts women buyers. Punchline: As the entire grocery store becomes protein-washed, ingredient quality is a bigger buying factor. Trading fortified formulas for whole foods, WILDE is bringing more substance to the snack aisle. October 22, 2026 Jewelry-Inspired Wearables Blend Fashion and Function Statement piece.
